text:
maya_eng: Quick Q — re: async job endpoints for long-running work. Current flow: POST /jobs -> 202 + job_id, client polls /jobs/:id. I want to nail down a few edge cases before I update the spec: heartbeat/lease model for workers, how cancels race with in-progress work, and what fields we return for clients to reason about liveness. cc @owen_platform @lucy_sre

owen_platform: Short answers up front: (1) expose lease_expires_at on status (ISO8601) updated by the runtime when a worker claims/extends a lease; (2) add last_seen so clients can see when the runtime actually observed activity; (3) return Retry-After in the 202 to help clients backoff.

lucy_sre: +1 on lease_expires_at. For cancel semantics we should set state=cancel_requested on cancel API and let workers poll that. If worker already running, outcome can be cancelled or completed; we need a documented tie-breaker. Also: don't hard-delete jobs on cancel.

ben_api: Also: POST /jobs must accept Idempotency-Key header and dedupe. Behavior proposal: if the key maps to an existing job, return 202 with the existing job id (not a 409). That keeps retries simple for clients.

maya_eng: Thinking about worker API: worker PATCH /jobs/:id/lease {worker_id, extend_seconds}. Worker gets the lease_expires_at back. If worker dies, runtime will requeue after lease expiry. Clients that enqueue jobs don't need to heartbeat. Workers do.

owen_platform: Another small UX win: when we return 202 include Location: /jobs/:id and Retry-After: 3 (or whatever suggestion) so clients don't hammer. Also add a header X-Job-Lease (optional) for workers when they claim.

carla_pm: From product side we want a client-level deadline param: e.g. client_deadline_seconds on POST. If job can't finish in that window, runtime should mark timed_out and surface that. Need clear metrics too.

lucy_sre: Proposed minimal status schema (for spec). Keep fields explicit so SDKs can rely on them:
```json
{
  "id":"job_123",
  "state":"queued|running|complete|error|cancel_requested|cancelled|timed_out",
  "lease_expires_at":"2025-03-25T12:34:56Z",
  "last_seen":"2025-03-25T12:30:01Z",
  "result_url":"/jobs/123/result",
  "error_code":"optional_string"
}
```

maya_eng: Nice. One tricky race: worker finishes and writes final result just as client sends cancel. How do we deterministically pick winner? We need something simple and reliable. Ideas?

owen_platform: Full causal system is heavy. Two pragmatic options: (A) server monotonic event counter that ordering uses (requires worker to include seen counter) or (B) a small grace_window: if worker completion_time <= cancel_request_time + grace_window, accept worker result. B is simpler.

ben_api: I vote for grace_window (configurable, default 2s). Document it clearly. Also make sure workers set a precise completion_time (ISO8601 with ms) in their final write so comparison is deterministic.

maya_eng: Agree on grace_window. We'll document default and make it overridable per deployment. Also we should add a cancellation sub-state: cancel_pending vs cancelled — cancel_pending indicates a cancel request exists but worker might still finish within grace window.

owen_platform: I'll draft the PR updating the API spec + runtime behavior. I'll include unit tests for: lease expiry -> requeue, cancel before start -> immediate cancelled, cancel during running -> respect grace_window.

carla_pm: Timeline: if PR lands by EOD I'll review, otherwise Monday. :eyes:

ci-bot: CI: specs/job-api#482 — tests passed :white_check_mark:

maya_eng: Thanks everyone. I'll sketch the example responses + sample SDK usage and drop in the PR description. If people want to call out other edge cases (retries with idempotency, partial results, streaming updates) add them to the PR comments.
